scene.label: Act 1, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Tyre. A room in the palace.
scene.location: Tyre. A room in the palace.

lines.text: [To Lords without.] Let none disturb us.—Why should this change of thoughts,
lines.plainText: To Lords without Let none disturb usWhy should this change of thoughts

lines.text: The sad companion, dull-eyed melancholy,
lines.plainText: The sad companion dulleyed melancholy

lines.text: Be my so used a guest as not an hour
lines.plainText: Be my so used a guest as not an hour

lines.text: In the day's glorious walk or peaceful night,
lines.plainText: In the day's glorious walk or peaceful night

lines.text: The tomb where grief should sleep, can breed me quiet?
lines.plainText: The tomb where grief should sleep can breed me quiet

lines.text: Here pleasures court mine eyes, and mine eyes shun them,
lines.plainText: Here pleasures court mine eyes and mine eyes shun them

lines.text: And danger, which I fear'd, is at Antioch,
lines.plainText: And danger which I fear'd is at Antioch

lines.text: Whose arm seems far too short to hit me here:
lines.plainText: Whose arm seems far too short to hit me here

lines.text: Yet neither pleasure's art can joy my spirits,
lines.plainText: Yet neither pleasure's art can joy my spirits

lines.text: Nor yet the other's distance comfort me.
lines.plainText: Nor yet the other's distance comfort me

lines.text: Then it is thus: the passions of the mind,
lines.plainText: Then it is thus the passions of the mind

lines.text: That have their first conception by misdread,
lines.plainText: That have their first conception by misdread

lines.text: Have after-nourishment and life by care;
lines.plainText: Have afternourishment and life by care

lines.text: And what was first but fear what might be done,
lines.plainText: And what was first but fear what might be done

lines.text: Grows elder now and cares it be not done.
lines.plainText: Grows elder now and cares it be not done

lines.text: And so with me: the great Antiochus,
lines.plainText: And so with me the great Antiochus

lines.text: 'Gainst whom I am too little to contend,
lines.plainText: 'Gainst whom I am too little to contend

lines.text: Since he's so great can make his will his act,
lines.plainText: Since he's so great can make his will his act

lines.text: Will think me speaking, though I swear to silence;
lines.plainText: Will think me speaking though I swear to silence

lines.text: Nor boots it me to say I honour him.
lines.plainText: Nor boots it me to say I honour him

lines.text: If he suspect I may dishonour him:
lines.plainText: If he suspect I may dishonour him

lines.text: And what may make him blush in being known,
lines.plainText: And what may make him blush in being known

lines.text: He'll stop the course by which it might be known;
lines.plainText: He'll stop the course by which it might be known

lines.text: With hostile forces he'll o'erspread the land,
lines.plainText: With hostile forces he'll o'erspread the land

lines.text: And with the ostent of war will look so huge,
lines.plainText: And with the ostent of war will look so huge

lines.text: Amazement shall drive courage from the state;
lines.plainText: Amazement shall drive courage from the state

lines.text: Our men be vanquish'd ere they do resist,
lines.plainText: Our men be vanquish'd ere they do resist

lines.text: And subjects punish'd that ne'er thought offence:
lines.plainText: And subjects punish'd that ne'er thought offence

lines.text: Which care of them, not pity of myself,
lines.plainText: Which care of them not pity of myself

lines.text: Who am no more but as the tops of trees,
lines.plainText: Who am no more but as the tops of trees

lines.text: Which fence the roots they grow by and defend them,
lines.plainText: Which fence the roots they grow by and defend them

lines.text: Makes both my body pine and soul to languish,
lines.plainText: Makes both my body pine and soul to languish

lines.text: And punish that before that he would punish.
lines.plainText: And punish that before that he would punish

lines.text: Joy and all comfort in your sacred breast!
lines.plainText: Joy and all comfort in your sacred breast

lines.text: And keep your mind, till you return to us,
lines.plainText: And keep your mind till you return to us

lines.text: Peaceful and comfortable!
lines.plainText: Peaceful and comfortable

lines.text: Peace, peace, and give experience tongue.
lines.plainText: Peace peace and give experience tongue

lines.text: They do abuse the king that flatter him:
lines.plainText: They do abuse the king that flatter him

lines.text: For flattery is the bellows blows up sin;
lines.plainText: For flattery is the bellows blows up sin

lines.text: The thing the which is flatter'd, but a spark,
lines.plainText: The thing the which is flatter'd but a spark

lines.text: To which that spark gives heat and stronger glowing:
lines.plainText: To which that spark gives heat and stronger glowing

lines.text: Whereas reproof, obedient and in order,
lines.plainText: Whereas reproof obedient and in order

lines.text: Fits kings, as they are men, for they may err.
lines.plainText: Fits kings as they are men for they may err

lines.text: When Signior Sooth here does proclaim peace,
lines.plainText: When Signior Sooth here does proclaim peace

lines.text: He flatters you, makes war upon your life.
lines.plainText: He flatters you makes war upon your life

lines.text: Prince, pardon me, or strike me, if you please;
lines.plainText: Prince pardon me or strike me if you please

lines.text: I cannot be much lower than my knees.
lines.plainText: I cannot be much lower than my knees

lines.text: All leave us else, but let your cares o'erlook
lines.plainText: All leave us else but let your cares o'erlook

lines.text: What shipping and what lading's in our haven,
lines.plainText: What shipping and what lading's in our haven

lines.text: And then return to us.
lines.plainText: And then return to us

lines.text: An angry brow, dread lord.
lines.plainText: An angry brow dread lord

lines.text: If there be such a dart in princes' frowns,
lines.plainText: If there be such a dart in princes' frowns

lines.text: How durst thy tongue move anger to our face?
lines.plainText: How durst thy tongue move anger to our face

lines.text: How dares the plants look up to heaven, from whence
lines.plainText: How dares the plants look up to heaven from whence

lines.text: They have their nourishment?
lines.plainText: They have their nourishment

lines.text: Thou know'st I have power
lines.plainText: Thou know'st I have power

lines.text: To take thy life from thee.
lines.plainText: To take thy life from thee

lines.text: Rise, prithee, rise.
lines.plainText: Rise prithee rise

lines.text: Sit down: thou art no flatterer:
lines.plainText: Sit down thou art no flatterer

lines.text: I thank thee for it; and heaven forbid
lines.plainText: I thank thee for it and heaven forbid

lines.text: That kings should let their ears hear their faults hid!
lines.plainText: That kings should let their ears hear their faults hid

lines.text: Fit counsellor and servant for a prince,
lines.plainText: Fit counsellor and servant for a prince

lines.text: Who by thy wisdom makest a prince thy servant,
lines.plainText: Who by thy wisdom makest a prince thy servant

lines.text: What wouldst thou have me do?
lines.plainText: What wouldst thou have me do

lines.text: To bear with patience
lines.plainText: To bear with patience

lines.text: Such griefs as you yourself do lay upon yourself.
lines.plainText: Such griefs as you yourself do lay upon yourself

lines.text: Thou speak'st like a physician, Helicanus,
lines.plainText: Thou speak'st like a physician Helicanus

lines.text: That ministers a potion unto me
lines.plainText: That ministers a potion unto me

lines.text: That thou wouldst tremble to receive thyself.
lines.plainText: That thou wouldst tremble to receive thyself

lines.text: Attend me, then: I went to Antioch,
lines.plainText: Attend me then I went to Antioch

lines.text: Where, as thou know'st, against the face of death,
lines.plainText: Where as thou know'st against the face of death

lines.text: I sought the purchase of a glorious beauty,
lines.plainText: I sought the purchase of a glorious beauty

lines.text: From whence an issue I might propagate,
lines.plainText: From whence an issue I might propagate

lines.text: Are arms to princes, and bring joys to subjects.
lines.plainText: Are arms to princes and bring joys to subjects

lines.text: Her face was to mine eye beyond all wonder;
lines.plainText: Her face was to mine eye beyond all wonder

lines.text: The rest—hark in thine ear—as black as incest,
lines.plainText: The resthark in thine earas black as incest

lines.text: Which by my knowledge found, the sinful father
lines.plainText: Which by my knowledge found the sinful father

lines.text: Seem'd not to strike, but smooth: but thou know'st this,
lines.plainText: Seem'd not to strike but smooth but thou know'st this

lines.text: 'Tis time to fear when tyrants seems to kiss.
lines.plainText: 'Tis time to fear when tyrants seems to kiss

lines.text: Which fear so grew in me I hither fled,
lines.plainText: Which fear so grew in me I hither fled

lines.text: Under the covering of a careful night,
lines.plainText: Under the covering of a careful night

lines.text: Who seem'd my good protector; and, being here,
lines.plainText: Who seem'd my good protector and being here

lines.text: Bethought me what was past, what might succeed.
lines.plainText: Bethought me what was past what might succeed

lines.text: I knew him tyrannous; and tyrants' fears
lines.plainText: I knew him tyrannous and tyrants' fears

lines.text: Decrease not, but grow faster than the years:
lines.plainText: Decrease not but grow faster than the years

lines.text: And should he doubt, as no doubt he doth,
lines.plainText: And should he doubt as no doubt he doth

lines.text: That I should open to the listening air
lines.plainText: That I should open to the listening air

lines.text: How many worthy princes' bloods were shed,
lines.plainText: How many worthy princes' bloods were shed

lines.text: To keep his bed of blackness unlaid ope,
lines.plainText: To keep his bed of blackness unlaid ope

lines.text: To lop that doubt, he'll fill this land with arms,
lines.plainText: To lop that doubt he'll fill this land with arms

lines.text: And make pretence of wrong that I have done him;
lines.plainText: And make pretence of wrong that I have done him

lines.text: When all, for mine, if I may call offence,
lines.plainText: When all for mine if I may call offence

lines.text: Must feel war's blow, who spares not innocence:
lines.plainText: Must feel war's blow who spares not innocence

lines.text: Which love to all, of which thyself art one,
lines.plainText: Which love to all of which thyself art one

lines.text: Who now reprovest me for it,—
lines.plainText: Who now reprovest me for it

lines.text: Alas, sir!
lines.plainText: Alas sir

lines.text: Drew sleep out of mine eyes, blood from my cheeks,
lines.plainText: Drew sleep out of mine eyes blood from my cheeks

lines.text: Musings into my mind, with thousand doubts
lines.plainText: Musings into my mind with thousand doubts

lines.text: How I might stop this tempest ere it came;
lines.plainText: How I might stop this tempest ere it came

lines.text: And finding little comfort to relieve them,
lines.plainText: And finding little comfort to relieve them

lines.text: I thought it princely charity to grieve them.
lines.plainText: I thought it princely charity to grieve them

lines.text: Well, my lord, since you have given me leave to speak,
lines.plainText: Well my lord since you have given me leave to speak

lines.text: Freely will I speak. Antiochus you fear,
lines.plainText: Freely will I speak Antiochus you fear

lines.text: And justly too, I think, you fear the tyrant,
lines.plainText: And justly too I think you fear the tyrant

lines.text: Who either by public war or private treason
lines.plainText: Who either by public war or private treason

lines.text: Will take away your life.
lines.plainText: Will take away your life

lines.text: Therefore, my lord, go travel for a while,
lines.plainText: Therefore my lord go travel for a while

lines.text: Till that his rage and anger be forgot,
lines.plainText: Till that his rage and anger be forgot

lines.text: Or till the Destinies do cut his thread of life.
lines.plainText: Or till the Destinies do cut his thread of life

lines.text: Your rule direct to any; if to me,
lines.plainText: Your rule direct to any if to me

lines.text: Day serves not light more faithful than I'll be.
lines.plainText: Day serves not light more faithful than I'll be

lines.text: I do not doubt thy faith;
lines.plainText: I do not doubt thy faith

lines.text: But should he wrong my liberties in my absence?
lines.plainText: But should he wrong my liberties in my absence

lines.text: We'll mingle our bloods together in the earth,
lines.plainText: We'll mingle our bloods together in the earth

lines.text: From whence we had our being and our birth.
lines.plainText: From whence we had our being and our birth

lines.text: Tyre, I now look from thee then, and to Tarsus
lines.plainText: Tyre I now look from thee then and to Tarsus

lines.text: Intend my travel, where I'll hear from thee;
lines.plainText: Intend my travel where I'll hear from thee

lines.text: And by whose letters I'll dispose myself.
lines.plainText: And by whose letters I'll dispose myself

lines.text: The care I had and have of subjects' good
lines.plainText: The care I had and have of subjects' good

lines.text: On thee I lay, whose wisdom's strength can bear it.
lines.plainText: On thee I lay whose wisdom's strength can bear it

lines.text: I'll take thy word for faith, not ask thine oath:
lines.plainText: I'll take thy word for faith not ask thine oath

lines.text: Who shuns not to break one will sure crack both:
lines.plainText: Who shuns not to break one will sure crack both

lines.text: But in our orbs we'll live so round and safe,
lines.plainText: But in our orbs we'll live so round and safe

lines.text: That time of both this truth shall ne'er convince,
lines.plainText: That time of both this truth shall ne'er convince

lines.text: Thou show'dst a subject's shine, I a true prince.
lines.plainText: Thou show'dst a subject's shine I a true prince
